analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md covering lines 1-797 (Nemotron Super local owner, managed slot, GLM5Next). The recorded diff hunk is at head lines 2058-2073 (Flint KV/paged policy) and falls outside the supplied excerpts, so the actual changed text was only seen as a truncated patch. This is a documentation-only change. I found no code, endpoint or control change in the visible material, so no security regression is visible.

The visible patch says Flint is forced to native KV and checkpoint precision, ignoring provider-wide defaults, and that explicit non-native selections are refused. It also says the automatic KV backend is treated as explicit paged for a verified FlintModel, with a refused load on contiguous, the paged kill switch or a capability veto. That reads as stricter fail-closed behaviour, not a weakening.

In the visible excerpts I checked the prefix-cache descriptions against T-041. Text prefix reuse for Super is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope. Without a scope it stays cold and never publishes. The managed slot emits no cache receipts or cache capability. The in-memory checkpoint bank is resident RAM and not on the SSD tier. This is consistent with T-041's scoping and SEC-035 posture, and no new at-rest artifact appears. The media-admission, memory-reservation and 429/503 refusal descriptions are availability controls, and none contradicts the threat model.

Remaining uncertainties: the description of Flint paged enforcement and the Nemotron/GLM behaviours cannot be verified against the underlying Swift sources, which were not supplied. The truncated patch (patch_excerpt_complete=false) leaves the tail of the Flint hunk unseen. The next pass should confirm that the code in EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend and EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve matches the documented behaviour.
